lessons.culture: Beirut flats are rented by the month, often quoted in dollars, and a deposit of about one month's rent (ta2meen) with a written 3a2d eejaar is usual. Always ask what the rent includes, especially water and electricity (including any private generator subscription).

lessons.culture: A small repair is often a favour from a relative or neighbour first, and he is thanked with "ya3Teek el-3aafye"; a plumber is a sankari and an electrician a kahraba2i, and it is polite to ask the cost before the work starts. Power cuts are common in Lebanon, so "el-kahraba 2aaT3a" is an ordinary thing to hear, and people say al-7amdu lillaah when a job ends well.

lessons.culture: In Islam a neighbour has a great right, and neighbours share food, visit each other when ill and avoid disturbing each other with noise. challenge.title: Viewing a Flat
challenge.instructions: Write and act out a conversation of at least 10 lines where you ask about a flat for rent, its rent, bedrooms and floor, ask whether it is furnished and whether water and electricity are included, ask to view it, and say what you decide. Use at least 8 target phrases from Unit 18.
required_elements: A question about the rent or the bedrooms with قدّيش.
A question about the floor or the lift, using بأيّا طابق or في أسانسير.
A question about whether water and electricity are included, or whether the flat is furnished.
A request to see the flat with فيني.
A closing decision with رح آخدها or بدّي عقد إيجار.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: مرحبا. عَم فَتِّش عَلى شَقّة لِلإيجار. قَدّيش الإيجار بِالشَّهر؟
dialogue.transliteration: mar7aba. 3am fattesh 3ala sha22a lal-eejaar. 2addeesh el-eejaar bish-shahr?
dialogue.english: Hello. I am looking for a flat to rent. How much is the rent per month?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: أَهلين. ألف دولار بِالشَّهر، وفيها تْلات أُوَض نوم.
dialogue.transliteration: ahleen. elf dolaar bish-shahr, w feeha tlet owaD noom.
dialogue.english: Welcome. A thousand dollars a month, and it has three bedrooms.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Which floor? And is there a lift?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: بِالطّابِق التّاني، وإيه، في أَسَانْسور بِالبِناية.
dialogue.transliteration: bet-Taabe2 et-taani, w eh, fee asansoor bel-binaaye.
dialogue.english: On the second floor, and yes, the building has a lift.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Are water and electricity included in the rent?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: لأ، بْتِدفَعُن إِنتَ. فيك تْشوف الشَّقّة هَلَّق إذا بَدَّك.
dialogue.transliteration: la2, btedfa3on ente. feek tshuuf esh-sha22a halla2 iza baddak.
dialogue.english: No, you pay for them. You can see the flat now if you like.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Yes, I would like to. Is the flat furnished?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: تْفَضَّل. فيها عَفش كامِل، والمَطبَخ حَدّ الصّالون.
dialogue.transliteration: tfaDDal. feeha 3afsh kaamel, w el-maTbakh 7add eS-Saloon.
dialogue.english: Please come in. It has full furniture, and the kitchen is next to the living room.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: حِلْوِة كْتير. رَح آخِدها، وبَدّي عَقد إيجار لِسَنة.
dialogue.transliteration: 7elwe ktiir. ra7 aakhedha, w baddi 3a2d eejaar la-sane.
dialogue.english: Very nice. I will take it, and I want a one-year lease.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: تَمام، مَبروك. تَعا بُكرا نِكتُب العَقد.
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam, mabrouk. ta3a bukra nektob el-3a2d.
dialogue.english: Fine, congratulations. Come tomorrow and we will write the contract.
